h1: The 5 Best Metal Filing Cabinets for Home Offices and Under Desks, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Metal Filing Cabinets: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 locking metal filing cabinets for home offices, from 2-drawer vertical and lateral units to a 4-drawer anti-tip model.
summary: The Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet is the metal filing cabinet to buy for most home offices, arriving assembled with locking drawers and legal-size hanging file support. The Livofloral 4-drawer unit has the most capacity and an anti-tip design, the Letaya lateral suits wall-side spaces, and the SISESOL is the narrow pick for tight desk gaps.
intro: People buy a filing cabinet for the drawers and forget the rails. What decides whether a cabinet stays useful for ten years is how the drawer slides carry a full load of hanging folders, not the paint colour or the lock. A drawer that binds when it is half full is a drawer you stop using, and the pile on the desk comes back.

We reviewed eight listings, set aside a tall garage storage cabinet and a rolling unit with fabric drawer fronts that do not suit the metal-cabinet brief, and ranked the six remaining steel cabinets. The ranking rests on spec sheets and listings: drawer count, file size support, locks, footprint and assembly. Where a number is missing we leave it out. Price buckets replace exact prices.

products.name: Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock, Under Desk Metal Filing Cabinet for Home Office
products.verdict: Three locking drawers, fully assembled, rolling under a desk and holding letter, legal and A4 files.
products.description:
The Letaya is a mobile metal file cabinet with three drawers that lock and arrives fully assembled. It takes letter, legal and A4 hanging files and is sized to fit under a desk.

The assembled delivery is a larger advantage than it sounds, because assembling a filing cabinet with drawer slides is the most common source of crooked, sticking drawers. Three drawers give you separate homes for current work, tax records and reference papers. The casters let you roll it out for access, then tuck it away. The tradeoff is height: an under-desk unit has shallow drawers that hold fewer files than a tall cabinet.

Buy it if you have a regular desk and a modest paper trail. Skip it if you need a tall cabinet that holds years of records.
pros: Takes letter, legal and A4 files
Rolls out from under the desk
products.idealFor: Home offices with a regular desk and modest paperwork.
products.skipIf: You need to store years of records.

products.name: Livofloral Vertical File Cabinet with 4 Drawers and 1 Door, Metal, 2 Locks, Anti-Tip
products.verdict: Four drawers plus a door compartment, two locks and an anti-tip design, in white.
products.description:
This Livofloral cabinet stacks four drawers with a one-door compartment, uses two separate locks, adds an anti-tip design and supports letter, legal and A4 files. It comes in white and needs assembly.

Capacity is why it ranks so high. Four drawers handle a full year of household or small business records, and the door compartment keeps binders and supplies out of sight. The anti-tip design matters on a tall cabinet: a tall unit with several full drawers open can topple, and an anti-tip mechanism stops more than one drawer opening at once. Two locks let you secure the file drawers and the cupboard separately. The cost is a bigger footprint and the assembly time.

Buy it if you have wall space and a lot of paper. The listing is newer, so expect less owner history than the established models.
pros: Four drawers plus a door compartment
Anti-tip design for a tall unit
products.idealFor: Busy home offices with lots of paperwork.

products.name: Letaya 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Metal Lateral Filing Cabinet for Home Office
products.verdict: A two-drawer lateral cabinet, 27.95 by 28.35 by 15.74 inches, for limited depth and spare wall width.
products.description:
The lateral Letaya has two locking drawers laid out side to side, with hanging file support for letter, legal and A4. It measures 27.95 inches high, 28.35 wide and 15.74 deep.

A lateral design files folders left to right instead of front to back, so the cabinet is shallow but wide. That suits a room where you lack front-to-back depth but have spare wall. It can also serve as a low credenza top. The tradeoff is that lateral drawers need space to pull open sideways in your viewing line, and a wider cabinet is heavier to move once it is loaded.

Choose it when depth is your constraint. If you have more depth than width, a standard vertical unit stores more per square inch of floor.
pros: Can double as a low credenza
products.idealFor: Rooms with spare wall but little depth.

products.name: BYNSOE 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Vertical Filing Storage Cabinet, Steel
products.verdict: A standard locked steel two-drawer vertical cabinet that takes letter-size files, with assembly required.
products.description:
The BYNSOE is a two-drawer vertical steel cabinet with locking drawers. It is rated for letter-size files and needs assembly.

It earns its fourth spot for being the plain, familiar shape, which works in most rooms. Two drawers stacked vertically give you a decent amount of file space on a small footprint, and steel is the right material for a cabinet that must stand up to years of use. The listing names only letter size, so legal-size paper may not fit, which sets it behind the Letaya models. Assembly is on you, and it is worth taking time to align the slides.

Buy it if your files are letter size and you want a straightforward locked cabinet. Skip it if you keep legal documents.
products.idealFor: Letter-size filing in a small space.

products.name: SISESOL 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Narrow Vertical Filing Cabinet, Under Desk
products.verdict: A narrow black metal cabinet with a lock and letter, A4 and legal support, under $50.
products.description:
The SISESOL is a narrow two-drawer vertical cabinet with locking drawers and a black metal finish. It supports letter, A4 and legal files and goes together with easy assembly. It costs $25 to $50.

Its narrowness is the draw: a very tight gap beside a desk, between a desk and a wall or under a short desk is where a standard cabinet will not go. For the money you also get legal-size support and a lock, features that some wider units skip. The cost of a slim body is a smaller usable drawer, so capacity is limited, and a thin cabinet is lighter and can feel less planted when a drawer is open.

Buy it for a cramped office and light paperwork. Skip it if you want a drawer that holds a lot of files.

methodology.description: Two, three and four drawer cabinets in vertical, lateral and narrow layouts were compared for storage per square foot of floor.

methodology.title: File size support
methodology.description: We checked which cabinets list letter, legal and A4 hanging file support, since a mismatch is a common reason for returns.

methodology.title: Locks and safety
methodology.description: Drawer locks, separate cupboard locks and anti-tip design were weighed for security and for safety around children.

methodology.title: Footprint and mobility
methodology.description: Under-desk casters, narrow bodies and lateral shapes were assessed against typical home office space limits.

methodology.title: Assembly and listing clarity
methodology.description: Fully assembled delivery and a detailed spec sheet earned points, since the listing is the buyer's only guide.

whatMatters.detail: A full drawer of hanging folders is heavy, and slides decide whether it glides or binds. Look for ball-bearing or full-extension slides in the description, and for a stated load per drawer. A cabinet with no mention of slides is a gamble.

Letter is 8.5 by 11 inches, legal is longer and A4 is slightly narrower and taller. A cabinet must have rails that accept the folders you use. Check for the words letter, legal or A4 on the listing, and measure your longest folder.

A lock deters casual snooping, not a determined thief. A single lock that secures every drawer is convenient, and separate locks help if a cupboard holds different items. Keep the spare key somewhere other than the cabinet.

Tall cabinets with several loaded drawers can topple if more than one opens at once. An interlock or anti-tip system lets only one drawer open at a time. For homes with children, this is a safety feature worth having.

Measure width, depth and height, plus the room needed to pull a drawer open. Casters make an under-desk cabinet easy to move, but locking wheels keep it from creeping. A lateral cabinet needs width, and a vertical unit needs depth.

faq.q: Do metal filing cabinets fit legal-size files?
faq.a: Only if the listing says so. The Letaya models, SISESOL and Livofloral list legal support, while the BYNSOE names letter only. Check your folders against the stated sizes before you order.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a file cabinet?
faq.a: Ignoring the depth needed to open a drawer. A cabinet that fits in the space may block the door or your chair when a drawer is pulled out. Measure the clearance, not just the footprint.

faq.q: Is the Letaya 3 Drawer worth it over a cheaper cabinet?
faq.a: Yes, if you value arriving assembled and legal-size support. Many cheaper cabinets need assembly and name fewer file sizes, and drawers that arrive aligned tend to stay smooth.
Plan for 30 to 60 minutes on cabinets that need building, and make sure the drawer slides are square before you tighten the screws. The Letaya 3 Drawer arrives fully assembled.
They deter casual access. A determined person can defeat a cabinet lock, so keep truly sensitive documents in a small safe. Store the spare key away from the cabinet.

faq.q: Can a filing cabinet tip over?
faq.a: Tall units with several loaded drawers can. Choose a model with an anti-tip design, as on the Livofloral, load the lower drawers first and never open more than one at a time.

finalTake: For most home offices, the Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet is the best metal filing cabinet, with locks, three drawers and no assembly. The Livofloral 4-drawer is the choice for lots of paper and an anti-tip design, the Letaya lateral works where depth is short, and the SISESOL fits the tightest gaps. Measure your space and your longest folder before you buy.
